card_roles.Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons: The mint, not the source: every -1/-1 counter you place buys a 1/1 deathtouch Snake, one per placement. Her combat trigger is a bonus on an unevasive 2/2 — do not attack into open blockers for one marginal counter.
card_roles.Yawgmoth, Thran Physician: The only mana-free sacrifice outlet here that also places a counter, which makes him the default tutor target. Always keep a second body on board: the ability carries one instance of "target", so an illegal target means no counter and no card.
card_roles.Mikaeus, the Unhallowed: Your only six-drop, and he places no counters himself. Cast him when Devoted Druid or Walking Ballista is already in play or in hand — alone he is an anthem and a small pile of undying triggers.
card_roles.Devoted Druid: Three green on the first pass and the one card that turns Mikaeus into a real loop. Without Mikaeus he is still a two-mana dork — play him on turn two and take the acceleration.
card_roles.Walking Ballista: Under Mikaeus with a free outlet it is the kill that needs no drain payoff at all. Alone, treat it as a scalable removal spell and spend counters on the creature actually attacking you.
card_roles.Blowfly Infestation: A repeatable counter source that feeds Hapatra every time a creature with a counter dies. Three of the deck's unsettled lines run through it — play it for the counters, not for a loop this manual has not verified.
card_roles.Nest of Scarabs: A second mint: your counter placements make 1/1 Insects as well as Snakes, so one sweeper pays twice. Deploy it before you cast Black Sun's Zenith, never after.
card_roles.Flourishing Defenses: The same exchange rate Nest of Scarabs gives you at three mana, for five, and it reads on any player's placement. Cast it when the cheap payoffs are already gone.
card_roles.Obelisk Spider: Your best converter: it drains each opponent on counter placement rather than on death, so a loop that places four counters per cycle pays four times. Fetch it first once a repeatable source is live.
card_roles.Zulaport Cutthroat: Table-wide drain on every creature you control dying, which is what turns a Snake wave into damage. Hold it as the converter for lines that run on a sacrifice outlet rather than on counters.
card_roles.Bastion of Remembrance: Zulaport on an enchantment that a creature wrath cannot touch, and it brings a body along. Lead with it against decks whose answers all point at creatures.
card_roles.Blood Artist: He drains one named player per death, so he is a value card and a wrath tax rather than a table clock. Take the life, and do not pivot on him alone.
card_roles.Skullclamp: Two cards for {1} on every 1/1 Snake — the best card-advantage engine in the deck by a distance. Clamp the token you were about to sacrifice anyway.
card_roles.Grim Haruspex: A card on every nontoken creature you control dying, which pays for Yawgmoth activations you were making regardless. He never sees your Snakes, so sequence him alongside real bodies.
card_roles.Morbid Opportunist: One card per turn from anybody's creature dying, which is free income in a four-player game. It triggers once each turn — do not hold your sacrifices back trying to squeeze more out of it.
card_roles.Deadly Dispute: A spare body becomes two cards and a Treasure at instant speed. Cash a Snake in response to targeted removal rather than in your own main phase.
card_roles.Village Rites: One black mana, two cards, instant speed. It is the cheapest way to make a wrath cost your opponents something.
card_roles.Night's Whisper: Two cards for two mana with no board requirement at all. Cast it on the turn your board is empty — that is the turn nothing else here draws.
card_roles.The One Ring: A turn of protection plus an escalating draw engine, paid for in life you already spend freely. Cast it when you need the turn off, not as a generic four-drop.
card_roles.Demonic Tutor: Two mana, any card, no strings. Point it at a repeatable -1/-1 source unless the table is one turn from killing you.
card_roles.Grim Tutor: Demonic Tutor for one more mana and three life. Count the life first — Yawgmoth, Bitterblossom and three painlands are all billing the same total.
card_roles.Diabolic Intent: Any card for two mana and a creature you were going to sacrifice anyway. Feed it a Snake and the cost rounds to nothing.
card_roles.Vampiric Tutor: One mana at instant speed, and it costs you your next draw. Cast it on the opponent's end step so the card arrives on time.
card_roles.Imperial Seal: Vampiric Tutor at sorcery speed. Fire it on a turn you had spare mana, not on the turn you need the card in hand.
card_roles.Worldly Tutor: A creature to the top of your library for one green at instant speed. Yawgmoth and Devoted Druid are the two names it should be finding.
card_roles.Survival of the Fittest: Repeatable creature tutoring for one green a shot, and the discard is close to free with Phyrexian Reclamation in the graveyard. Use it on every turn with a spare mana.
card_roles.Green Sun's Zenith: It puts the creature onto the battlefield instead of into your hand — Devoted Druid at X=2, Ivy Lane Denizen at X=4. That tempo is why it beats a card tutor on a tight turn.
card_roles.Ashnod's Altar: A free outlet and two colourless per body, which is a wrath dodge and a burst of mana in one card. Beside Mikaeus it buys one extra death — sequence it as a value activation.
card_roles.Phyrexian Altar: The coloured version at one mana per creature, and the colour is what makes it the better card here. Same rule beside Mikaeus: value, not a loop.
card_roles.Carrion Feeder: A one-drop free outlet that grows on every sacrifice. It adds +1/+1 counters, which fights your own plan — feed it Snakes and keep it away from creatures you want dead.
card_roles.Viscera Seer: One mana, free outlet, and a scry per body smooths every draw you take. It is the outlet to deploy on turn one.
card_roles.Blasting Station: A free outlet that untaps whenever a creature enters, so a Snake wave becomes a damage wave. Point the damage at whoever is closest to winning.
card_roles.Yahenni, Undying Partisan: A free outlet on a hasty body that goes indestructible on demand — your cleanest answer to a removal spell aimed at your own board. Sacrifice a Snake in response and keep everything.
card_roles.Fume Spitter: One mana that sacrifices itself to place a counter: a Snake, a dead X/1 and a death trigger for {B}. Save it to kill a mana dork rather than spending it on turn one.
card_roles.Serrated Arrows: Three counters over three turns from an artifact most creature decks simply cannot answer. Spend them one per turn for three separate Hapatra triggers.
card_roles.Contagion Clasp: It enters placing a counter and then proliferates every turn for {4}. Value the proliferate as removal you can repeat — how many Snake triggers a single mass placement yields is not settled here.
card_roles.Grim Affliction: A counter plus a proliferate at instant speed: a Snake, a shrink and a Crumbling Ashes target all in one card. Cast it on a blocker, not on your own turn.
card_roles.Crumbling Ashes: It destroys a creature carrying a -1/-1 counter every upkeep, and this deck always has one available. It is your only repeatable answer to a recurring threat — mark the target the turn before.
card_roles.Black Sun's Zenith: One card that wipes, mints fresh Snakes off the same placement and arms Necroskitter. Pick the X that kills their board and accept that your Snakes go with it — the tokens you get back enter clean.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: The reset button, and the one sweeper that pays you nothing: -X/-X places no counters, so Hapatra, Nest of Scarabs and Necroskitter all stay silent. Cast it to survive, never to build.
card_roles.Necroskitter: Every creature an opponent controls that dies with a -1/-1 counter on it comes back under your control. Put counters on their board before you sweep, not after.
card_roles.Host of the Hereafter: It enters with two +1/+1 counters and moves counters off your dying creatures onto a creature you choose. The loop it is famous for is unresolved here — play it as a four-mana body that recycles counters.
card_roles.Ivy Lane Denizen: It puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature whenever another green creature you control enters, and every Snake is green. Aim those counters away from your own fodder, since they cancel the -1/-1 counters you are trying to place.
card_roles.Scurry Oak: Evolve plus a Squirrel on every batch of +1/+1 counters, and its pairing with Ivy Lane Denizen is the highest-bracket line in the deck. That line is unresolved — use the Oak as a token maker until a scenario says more.
card_roles.Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER // Sephiroth,: A sacrifice outlet that draws on entry and on attack, plus a drain on every other creature dying. Four of those drains in one turn transforms him, and a Snake wave can supply them.
card_roles.Pitiless Plunderer: A Treasure for every other creature you control dying, which is how a long sacrifice chain funds itself. Deploy it before the chain starts, not halfway through.
card_roles.Bitterblossom: A body every upkeep for one life, from an enchantment a creature wrath cannot touch. It is keepable on its own — it rebuilds your board without any other card.
card_roles.Eternal Witness: Any card back from the graveyard, attached to a body you can sacrifice afterwards. Rebuy the sweeper or the tutor, not a mana rock.
card_roles.Phyrexian Reclamation: Two life and {1}{B} returns any creature from your graveyard, every turn, at instant speed. It is your recursion engine and it is what makes Survival of the Fittest's discard free.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Hexproof and indestructible for your whole board at two mana. Hold it for the wrath or the mass bounce, not for one targeted removal spell.
card_roles.Lightning Greaves: Haste for zero, which is what restores the mana half of the Druid loop. The shroud also stops Hapatra and Yawgmoth targeting whatever it protects — move it off before you activate.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for {1} to equip, and the hexproof leaves your own targeting alone. Put these on the creature you still need to target.
card_roles.Orcish Bowmasters: Flash, a ping and an Army token, and every extra card an opponent draws pings again. Hold it up on their turn rather than casting it on yours.
card_roles.Birds of Paradise: A turn-one dork producing either of your colours, which casts Hapatra on turn two. Later it is a body worth sacrificing like any other.
card_roles.Llanowar Elves: One green on turn one, and fodder afterwards. Deploy it immediately — there is no turn where holding it is better.
card_roles.Elvish Mystic: Identical to Llanowar Elves and just as welcome. Two dorks in an opener means a turn-two commander plus a spell.
card_roles.Dark Ritual: Three black from one, which is a turn-one Bitterblossom or a turn-two Yawgmoth off two lands. Spend it on a permanent, not on a tutor.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless on turn one that nothing in your curve is too coloured to use. Cast it first, every time.
card_roles.Mana Vault: Three colourless now against an untap step later. Fire it on the turn you are deploying the engine, not on turn one for its own sake.
card_roles.Grim Monolith: Three colourless with a {4} untap this deck can afford in the late game. It buys turns, not fixing — it adds no coloured source at all.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Two mana for a rock that taps for either of your colours. It is the one artifact here doing fixing work; the rest are colourless.
card_roles.Lotus Petal: One mana of any colour, once, for free. Crack it on the turn the commander or a tutor is exactly one short.
card_roles.Chrome Mox: Free acceleration that eats a coloured card out of your hand. Only fire it when the hand has a genuine spare — in a two-land keep it usually does not.
card_roles.Mox Diamond: Free, and it taps for either colour, at the price of a land from hand. Thirty-six lands means you can usually pay that — but never from a two-lander.
card_roles.Fixing lands: Twenty-two of your twenty-four land entries make both colours and none of them enters tapped, so colour is almost never why a turn stalls. Play the painlands — City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Tarnished Citadel — while your life total is still fresh.
card_roles.Utility lands: Eight lands do a second job: Grim Backwoods converts a body into a card, Lazotep Quarry is an outlet and a late reanimator, Abstergo Entertainment exiles every graveyard including yours, Talon Gates of Madara phases out a creature, and Svogthos, the Restless Tomb becomes a threat when your board is gone. Activate them on turns you were not casting anything.
card_roles.Basic lands: Seven Swamps and seven Forests, the only fourteen sources in the deck that answer just one question. Lead on a basic when the painlands can wait a turn.

combo_lines.001:
The clause that decides this case is undying's own intervening "if": return it "if it had no +1/+1 counters on it" (CR 702.93a). Undying hands the creature back wearing exactly one such counter. The off-switch is inside the ability.

The claim on the record was that Hapatra supplies the reset. Counter annihilation is real and automatic — a permanent holding both kinds loses N of each as a state-based action (CR 704.5q). But her placement is a combat-damage trigger, put on the stack only when she connects (CR 113.3c), so it cannot be interleaved between sacrifices. Holding: the claim fails as written.

Two exhibits carry it further. A sacrificed Snake token ceases to exist in the state-based check that runs before its own undying trigger reaches the stack (CR 704.5d), so the token version produces zero iterations rather than infinite ones. For a nontoken body the count is one — the second sacrifice sends it to the graveyard wearing the counter undying gave it, and the intervening "if" is false.

That disposes of the altars by name. Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder and Blasting Station each buy exactly one extra death beside Mikaeus, and Yahenni, Undying Partisan sits in the same column. Carrion Feeder is worse than neutral on the record, since its own trigger adds +1/+1 counters. None of the six is a loop.

What survives is narrower and better documented. Mikaeus with Devoted Druid is unbounded in deaths, counters, Snakes and drain — but not in mana, because the returned Druid is a new object that has not been under your control since your turn began (CR 302.6). The simulation prices that pairing at 2.5% assembled unassisted, 31.7% with a tutor, mean turn 5.69.

Two further findings sit beside it. Mikaeus with Walking Ballista is genuinely unbounded and a three-card assembly, because layer 7c makes a counterless Ballista a 1/1 rather than a 0/0 and the death-by-last-counter pattern never fires (CR 613.4c). Yawgmoth loops for real and is bounded by the library his own mandatory draw empties (CR 104.3c).

The combo sheet claims nineteen two-card infinites in these colours. This record verifies one, downgrades a second to a three-card assembly, refutes six, and on the remaining eleven it is silent.

cover.identity: You are playing a converter, not a combo pile. Hapatra does not make -1/-1 counters at will — her first ability is a combat-damage trigger on an unevasive 2/2 — she monetises counters that *other* cards place, at a rate of one 1/1 deathtouch Snake per placement event. The 99 around her is built so that every counter becomes a body, every body becomes a card or a drain, and a narrow but genuine combo ceiling sits above a very strong grindy median.

how_it_wins:
The table counts the combo sheet in your colours and treats you like a fuse. Here is the truer read, and it is better news: Hapatra is a mint, not a source. Her combat trigger rides an unevasive 2/2 and is worth at most one extra counter per swing, so stop building turns around it. The half you actually play is the payout — every time you put -1/-1 counters on a creature she hands you a 1/1 deathtouch Snake.

So hunt sources, not payoffs. Eight sacrifice outlets in this deck cost no mana and exactly one of them, Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, also places a counter. You draw a tutor in 78.0% of games — point the first one at a repeatable source and never at a drain. Blowfly Infestation, Serrated Arrows, Contagion Clasp and Black Sun's Zenith are the same job on different bodies; cast whichever one this turn's mana can afford.

Most games you win by out-carding three people and then draining them, and that game assembles 67.2% of the time at mean turn 3.62. Pace for it. Clamp a Snake for two cards, cash a spare body to Deadly Dispute or Village Rites at instant speed, and let Grim Haruspex collect your creatures while Morbid Opportunist collects everyone else's. Every Snake you leave home blanks an attacker of any size, so the board that draws you cards is the board nobody wants to attack into.

The kill is one repeatable source plus one converter that hits all three seats, and you hold a converter in 51.9% of games. When the second half arrives, count the table's spent interaction and go — prefer Obelisk Spider, which drains on counter placement rather than on death and so pays four times per Druid cycle. Blood Artist names one player per death: take the value, do not call it a clock. One standing constraint on all of it — nothing in the 99 destroys an artifact, an enchantment or a land, so play around resolved permanents rather than planning to answer them.
mana_base:
Thirty-six lands across twenty-four entries, and zero of them enter tapped. Twenty-two make both colours; the other fourteen are basics, seven Swamps and seven Forests. That is a mana base with no tax on it — every land you draw works the turn it arrives.

Twenty-nine black sources and twenty-nine green from lands alone, against a target of twenty-two apiece. Seven over on both sides, which is why lands by themselves put each colour at 96.2% on curve. The 90% yardstick is usually the thing ramp exists to rescue; here it is cleared before a single rock is counted.

Now the disagreement an audit exists to find. Black carries 71.4% of the pip load — 40.0 pips over 34 cards, running as deep as triple black — while holding a 50% source share. Green carries 28.6%, 16.0 pips over 15 cards, on the same 50%. A twenty-one-point gap between what a colour asks and what it holds is normally an invoice, and it costs nothing here, because twenty-two of the lands answer either question.

Sixteen nonland producers finish the job: nine rocks, five dorks, two rituals. They lift on-curve to 98.8% black and 99.1% green and tilt the nonland source count green, ten to eight, because three of the five dorks make only green. Five of the rocks — Sol Ring, Mana Vault, Grim Monolith, Ashnod's Altar and Chrome Mox — score zero coloured sources under the unconditional-mana rule. They are buying turns, not colours.

None of it is free. City of Brass, Mana Confluence and Tarnished Citadel bill you in life; Forbidden Orchard hands an opponent a Spirit every time you tap it. Restricted mana: none — not one source here arrives with a spend-this-only clause. Zero taplands is an invoice paid on a life total, and the shape of the payoff is 2.464 mana on turn two, 6.15 by turn six, while the land-drop hit rate slides from 90.2% on turn three to 54.0% on turn six.
matchups:
Every opponent believes your removal count tells them what you can answer. Fourteen interactive copies inside a twenty-card suite sounds like plenty, and all of it points at creatures. Your interaction covers one permanent class of five, with artifact, enchantment, graveyard and land uncovered (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite). Sort every table by the permanent type that beats you, and you will know before turn one which seats you interact with and which you have to race.

Read the two half-patches before you write those classes off. Abstergo Entertainment exiles every graveyard when you pay three and exile it, and Talon Gates of Madara phases out a creature as it enters. Both are lands, both fire once, and neither touches an artifact or an enchantment — schedule them, do not hold them as answers.

Sweeper control believes you fold to a wrath. Wrong deck. Bitterblossom rebuilds every upkeep for a life, Skullclamp turns each dying 1/1 into two cards, Grim Haruspex collects the nontokens, and Blood Artist makes their sweeper a drain you get to aim (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math).

So deploy in waves and lead with the half you do not mind losing. Tokens and cheap counter sources first, the enabler in hand until the pivot. Assume the wrath, because across four players it is near-certain, and when it lands recast Hapatra for two and carry on.

Pick your own sweeper on purpose. Black Sun's Zenith puts counters on each creature: a Snake off the placement, food for Nest of Scarabs, and every opposing creature that dies with a counter handed to Necroskitter. Toxic Deluge places no counters and triggers none of that, so save it for the turn you need the board gone and the life is genuinely spare.

Stax and tax is the matchup that breadth number is describing. No artifact removal, no enchantment removal and no counterspell means the lock does not come off, so believe that on the turn it lands and stop burning turns hunting an answer you did not pack. Race it or politick it (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial).

Race with the half a tax piece cannot touch. Yawgmoth costs a life and a body and no mana, Bitterblossom triggers free on your upkeep, and Hapatra costs two and hits the table on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs. Get under the second and third lock pieces, then keep activating while everyone else recounts lands.

Politick with the truth, because it is the cheapest resource at the table. Say out loud that you are the seat with no answer to the Winter Orb, and ask the player holding the Krosan Grip to spend it (strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs). Keep the deal small, specific and expiring — one turn of your counters pointed elsewhere for one piece of enchantment removal.

The land class is the hole with no patch at all. An opposing Gaea's Cradle or Cabal Coffers pays its owner for the whole game and you will never remove it, so tax the player instead of the permanent: point the removal you do have at their bodies and the politics at their mana.

Combo decks believe you are a slow token deck worth ignoring. Agree with them and cash it. Do not try to interact with an artifact or enchantment kill, because nothing in this list touches one; against a creature-based combo, spend Grim Affliction, Fume Spitter, Serrated Arrows and Walking Ballista the moment their piece is live rather than holding them into the kill (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy).

Rank combo proximity above every board threat, and re-rank it at the start of every one of your turns.

Be honest about your own clock while you do it. A drain converter arrives at mean turn 3.34, the unresolved Blowfly pairing at mean turn 4.10 in 16.3% of games, and the verified Mikaeus and Devoted Druid line at mean turn 5.69 in 2.5%. Stop planning to out-race a dedicated combo deck on assembly and win the deflection instead — be the board nobody points interaction at, and go while three players watch each other (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

Aggro believes a board of 1/1s is free damage. It is a wall of deathtouch that blanks their attacks regardless of size, and one board answering three players' attack plans is advantage no removal count will ever show you (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). Keep the Snakes home, and stop swinging Hapatra into open blockers for one marginal trigger.

Spend life here on purpose rather than by accident. Yawgmoth, Phyrexian Reclamation, Bitterblossom, Toxic Deluge, City of Brass, Mana Confluence and Tarnished Citadel all bill the same total your engine runs on (strategy:life-as-resource). Pick the one opponent whose clock is actually real and defend against that one, not the table (strategy:multiplayer.pod-management).

Creature midrange is the seat this deck was built for, and the only matchup where your one covered class is the right one. Their removal is poor against tokens and their attacks are poor into deathtouch. Hold single-target removal until something is pointed at you, because every one-for-one you cast on sight profits two bystanders for free (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry).

Land Crumbling Ashes early here and let it grind. It destroys a creature carrying a -1/-1 counter at each of your upkeeps, from a permanent class fair creature decks mostly cannot answer. Seed it with Fume Spitter or Grim Affliction, and collect a Snake off every placement it makes.

Then win the long game with cards instead of combat. Skullclamp, Grim Haruspex, Morbid Opportunist, Deadly Dispute and Village Rites turn a stream of 1/1s into a stream of cards, and four-player games run long enough that the scaling engine is the default winning plan (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock).

Graveyard hate aimed at you is the cheapest of the four holes to live with. A Rest in Peace effect costs you Necroskitter, Phyrexian Reclamation and Eternal Witness and costs you nothing else, because Snakes, counters and drains never touch a graveyard. Keep playing at full speed and let the seat that spent a card on you feel good about it.

Aimed the other way it is a scheduled decision, not an answer you hold. Abstergo Entertainment is your only graveyard hate and it exiles itself to work, so against a reanimator seat play it as a land early, name the turn you intend to spend it, and spend it before their payoff rather than after (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy).
mulligan:
Everyone keeps the hand with Nest of Scarabs and Blood Artist in it. Do not be everyone. Those cards are exchange rates, and an exchange rate with nothing to exchange is a blank until the engine exists. Your keep test is one question: does this hand reach a repeatable -1/-1 source?

You can afford to be strict, because the deck is forgiving. You keep the first seven 79.9% of the time, average 0.243 mulligans, and put Hapatra on the table on turn two in 9,970 of 10,000 runs. A keep does not have to hold the engine — it has to cast the commander on schedule and dig for one.

Keep on sight: two to four lands casting Hapatra on turn two, plus any of Yawgmoth, Devoted Druid, Blowfly Infestation or a tutor. Keep the two-lander with Birds of Paradise, Llanowar Elves, Elvish Mystic, Sol Ring, Lotus Petal or Dark Ritual attached — that hand casts the commander a turn early with a spell left over. Keep Skullclamp beside any token maker. Keep Bitterblossom alone, because it makes a body every upkeep and rebuilds through a wrath by itself.

Ship the five-lander with no tutor and no dork. Four zero-drops, sixteen ones and nineteen twos means that hand is holding two cards it will never spend. Ship converters with no source — Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance are the classic trap keep. Ship hands built on Mikaeus alone; he is your only six-drop, he places no counters, and he needs a named partner to do anything.

Treat Scurry Oak, Ivy Lane Denizen and Host of the Hereafter as bodies rather than as routes, because the lines they are famous for are unsettled here and you do not mulligan toward something this manual will not assert. On the way to six, compress the whole test to two things: black mana on turn two, and one card that either places counters repeatedly or fetches one that does.
threat_assessment:
The table looks at a 2/2 legend and a pair of 1/1 tokens and files you under snake deck. Let them. That read is the most valuable thing you own, and it costs you nothing to keep until you choose to spend it.

Bank the turns it buys. Hapatra lands on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 goldfish runs, so stop deliberating over turn 2 and move that thinking to turn 3. A payoff joins her by mean turn 3.6 in 67.2% of games, so play the first four turns as the value deck the table already believes you are.

The second thing the table believes is the dangerous one, and it may have come from your own mouth. The combo sheet claims nineteen two-card infinites; stack 001 verifies one, Mikaeus alongside Devoted Druid, and refutes six outright. Never sell the nineteen in a Rule 0 conversation. Say bracket 4, say eleven Game Changers, say one verified line, and let the honesty buy you a seat the bigger number would have cost you.

Then play the refuted six exactly the way you describe them. With Mikaeus on board, sacrificing a body to Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer or Blasting Station buys one undying return and stops. Take the activation for what it is worth — a death trigger, a card, a Snake — and never announce it as a kill, never tap out for it, and never keep a hand because it contains one.

Price the verified pairing before you build a turn on it. Mikaeus with Devoted Druid assembles in 2.5% of games unassisted and 31.7% once a tutor is counted, at mean turn 5.69. So the plan is never "find Mikaeus" — it is find the tutor, then decide what the table lets you do with it.

Play the unresolved lines at the same discount. Blowfly Infestation, Scurry Oak and Host of the Hereafter are counter sources and boards first, so cast them for that. If a loop shows up, take it with a spare body and a land still untapped.

The Hapatra-and-Blowfly pairing arrives in 16.3% of games and 12.5% by turn 6. Treat every one of those as a bonus and steer nothing toward it — no mulligan, no tutor, no turn built on its arrival.

Three permanents flip you from ignored to archenemy, and Hapatra is none of them.

Yawgmoth is the first, because he is the only free repeatable counter source in the deck and the table's removal will find him the turn he resolves. Put him down with a second body already on the board and a turn that converts. Anything less spends your scarcest card for a single activation.

Mikaeus is the second, and he announces himself. Six mana against a mean 6.15 available on turn 6 means you tap low to cast the card everyone reads as the combo piece. Cast him with Devoted Druid or Walking Ballista already on the battlefield, or hold him and cast two other things instead.

The third signal is quiet, and it is the one that actually kills. A converter that drains every seat — Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance, Obelisk Spider — landing beside a repeatable source is your pivot trigger. You hold one in 51.9% of games and 41.5% by turn 6, so keep it in hand for that turn rather than deploying it early to be shot off the table.

Deploy Obelisk Spider last of those three. It drains on counter placement rather than on death, so it converts your fastest engine several times quicker and reads as a kill the moment it lands beside a source.

Sequence to keep the cover on. Lead with the token half — Bitterblossom, Snakes, cheap counter sources — because it reads defensive and rebuilds through a wrath by itself. Hold the enabler until the window. Deploy fast mana on the turn it buys a threat, not on turn one for the look of it.

Know exactly what spends the cover: eleven Game Changers. Chrome Mox, Mox Diamond, Mana Vault, Grim Monolith, Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal, Worldly Tutor, Survival of the Fittest, Orcish Bowmasters, The One Ring. The turn one of those resolves your Snakes stop reading as chump blockers, so fire tutors on a turn when a louder seat has just done something (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

You draw a tutor in 78.0% of games and 67.6% by turn 6. Point the first one at a repeatable counter source, never at a converter — the converter class is four cards deep and shows up on its own in 51.9% of games, and the source class is two deep (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors).

The One Ring is the loudest card in this list. Cast it for the cards, on a turn you can afford both the life and the attention, and never as a protection turn you are hoping nobody prices.

When you take the archenemy seat, take it once and take it counted. Count open mana at every seat before you commit, and assume every held answer appears the moment you present the loop (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Prefer the attempt that leaves Bitterblossom, a converter and a board of Snakes behind if it fails.

A thin verified record is an advantage the moment you play to it. Three opponents will hold up mana against nineteen infinites the record credits you with exactly one of, and you get to spend that discount on every value turn in between. Pace for the median and hold the ceiling as opportunism (strategy:critical-mass) — this deck wins far more games by out-drawing the table than by ever finding a loop.

Eleven thousand seven hundred and ninety-nine eligible green-black cards, and ten of them made the list. Four aim at a single number, which tells you how far out of line that number is.

Interaction here answers one permanent class out of five. Beast Within at EDHREC rank 25 and Assassin's Trophy at 124 are the catch-alls; Nature's Claim comes in at one mana, and Scavenging Ooze at rank 1,570 is the graveyard answer. Forty per cent of a ten spent on one axis is unusual. So is a one-out-of-five.

The second cluster is a redundancy figure. Two of the deck's declared kill lines rest on a component of exactly one card, and one named card is 7.1% of an opening seven — Mikaeus plus Devoted Druid measures 2.5% assembled on its own and 31.7% once a tutor is counted, the widest gap on the board. Gravecrawler at rank 687, Reassembling Skeleton at 767 and Forsaken Miner at 2,465 are all recurring nontoken bodies, the cheapest of them one mana.

The funding is visible in the ramp column, which sits at sixteen copies against a 10-12 target — four of the ten cuts come from there rather than from anything doing engine work. The bracket floor reads 4 before and 4 after on all ten. These are extensions of the deck, not escalations of it.

One search came back empty, and it is the one worth flagging. The thinnest component of all is Blowfly Infestation at 16.3% assembled, and the closer pass found nothing for it — no combo line, no shared role signature, nothing across all 11,799 cards. Worth knowing before the ten below start reading as comprehensive.

Three famous names lose on arithmetic. The Great Henge ranks 235 and prices off greatest power, which on a board of 1/1 Snakes leaves it near nine mana. Peer into the Abyss costs seven in a deck whose modal cost is two. Triskelion wants a partner for a line Walking Ballista already covers.
